rationale: The plan is tightly bound to this dataset: it puts sex (factor) and age (centered, continuous) in the design ahead of condition, names the contrast c("condition","treated","control") with control releveled as reference, and — crucially for the stated age imbalance — devotes a QC step to quantifying confounding (age by group with a test, sex x condition table, covariate association with PC1-PC4, VIF and residual df) and requires an explicit verdict on identifiability. Normalization stays inside the model (median-of-ratios, TMM for the edgeR cross-check) with an explicit prohibition on residualizing counts for sex/age; the filter (>=10 counts in >=6 samples, smallest group size) is minimal and justified, and BH at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering, apeglm shrinkage on the condition coefficient, and no post-hoc LFC cut are all correctly specified. QC covers PCA colored by condition/sex/age, distance heatmap, library sizes and a flag-not-drop outlier policy, but it stops short of the reference's explicit XIST/Y-linked sex check — sex-linked genes appear only as an interpretive caveat in the DE step. Enrichment is not strictly required by the question but is well-specified (full ranked list on the Wald stat, tested-gene universe, named collections with a stated Reactome substitution, 15-500 window, ORA gated at 50 genes); the report step is exemplary on versions, thresholds, tested/DE counts, adjusted-vs-unadjusted comparison and design limitations.
